messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected on continuous-batching serving path (streaming RPCs). alert_id=ALRT-7321 link=https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/serve/cont-batch?orgId=1 

ops-bot: symptoms: p95->300ms (ok), p99->1600ms (breach), streaming stalls observed, increased packer queue depth. Affected region: us-west-2. Paging eng-oncall. :rotating_light:

carla: ack. i'm onpager. grabbing graphs now. rough ETA 5m for quick triage.

dinesh: i'm looking. based on the traces: large sequences (~>2k tokens) are getting packed with small sequences creating long-running batches. KV-cache eviction spikes at the same time (cache-miss-rate up ~3x). scheduling fairness shows a single tenant's long-reqs occupying GPU for extended windows.

sara: customer-impact? any 5xxs or streaming disconnects?

leo: 5xxs not increased yet, but streaming stall rate (stall events per 1000 requests) up 4x for customers using long-document summarization. Some clients reported noticeable slow responses.

carla: jotted SLOs: p95 target 300ms, p99 target 800ms. current p99 1.6s. need fast mitigation to avoid customer escalations.

dinesh: mitigation options: 1) reduce max_batch_size for streaming packer, 2) enforce batch size by byte/seq-length caps, 3) enable preemptive-shedding for very long sequences, 4) route streaming traffic for high-latency tenants to a smaller / faster quantized variant. recommend quick: reduce max_batch_size and enable per-request seq-length cap.

carla: do it. i can push quick config change to us-west-2 packer group. doing safe guard rollback in case of regressions.

carla: command: ```
# reduce streaming packer max batch size
redwoodctl config set serving.packers.streaming.max_batch_size 8 --region=us-west-2 --apply-now
```

ops-bot: DEPLOY JOB started by carla (job_id=JB-9943). watch: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/JB-9943

leo: running a canary baseline: switching 10% of streaming traffic to the reduced-batch config first. will observe 2m windows.

maria: FYI, i pushed a temporary rule in the scheduler to prioritize smaller seqs until we confirm, small change, low risk.

dinesh: initial telemetry after config change (2m): median batch size dropped from 18->6, p99 dropped 1.6s->780ms, p95 stayed ~320ms. KV cache-miss rate down ~35%. looks promising.

carla: good. bump canary to 50% and continue monitoring. if p99 stays <900ms after 5m, roll to 100%.

ops-bot: CANARY UPDATE: 50% traffic on reduced-batch config.

leo: after 7m at 50%: p99 across region = 740ms, streaming stalls decreased. no 5xx spike. customer feedback quiet for now.

maria: one observation: this will increase GPU utilization slightly (smaller batches = less throughput). capacity headroom in us-west-2 is ~18% so ok for now. note that cost/unit may go up if sustained.

carla: rolling to 100% now. command: ```
redwoodctl rollout apply JB-9943 --to=100% --region=us-west-2
```

ops-bot: ROLLOUT COMPLETE: config applied to all streaming packers in us-west-2. job=JB-9943

dinesh: post-rollout numbers (3m): p99=700ms, p95=310ms, batch median=5. KV-cache-miss trending down. scheduling fairness metrics show reduced skew; preempt events down.

sara: any customer-facing impact we should notify about? did any critical customer see errors?

leo: no increase in error-rate. a handful of latency-sensitive customers saw p99 drop into SLO but some throughput-heavy customers may see slightly higher per-token latencies overall. recommend proactive note to top-10 streaming customers: short status and measures taken.

maria: opened tracking ticket INFRA-1282 for permanent controls: adaptive batch sizing by seq-length, tenant-aware fair packing, and early-shed policy for very long streams.

carla: summary for handoff: incident: tail latency spike due to packer mixing long + short sequences leading to long batches and KV-cache thrash. mitigation: reduced streaming max_batch_size (8) + temporary scheduler bias to prefer small seqs. effect: p99 from 1600ms -> ~700ms, no increase in 5xxs. follow-ups: INFRA-1282 (adaptive packing), add per-tenant rate cap for long-streams, and add an alert for packer batch-size median >12.

carla: handing off to next on-call Jordan for monitoring: please watch p99 for 1h and escalate to infra lead if p99 >900ms for >5m. tagging you @jordan. :pray:

jordan: taking it. I'll keep eyes on the dashboard and ensure INFRA-1282 is owned. quick question: should i rollback if GPU utilization >80% for >10m?

maria: yes, if utilization sustained >80% and p99 still >900ms, revert to previous packer config and open escalation to capacity team. rollback command: ```
redwoodctl rollout revert JB-9943 --to=prev --region=us-west-2
```

jordan: noted. will monitor. thanks team. closing live incident thread, will update if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated): ALRT-7321 closed by carla. final snapshot: p99=700ms, p95=310ms, no 5xx increase. mitigation window started 1719999999 and resolved by 1720000450.
